finite_rx_bias.limit_basis: Ten shared bias-current units; engineering probe, not measured output capacity.
finite_rx_bias.input_loading: Retained split resistors at half the shared differential match. Conservative DC/common-mode fixture, not implemented common-source LNA impedance.
finite_rx_bias.scope: Supply-connected bounded behavioral driver; no loop bandwidth, quiescent current, reverse diode paths or transistor-level power-off proof.

common_mode_envelope.scope: Same connected circuit and external network; carrier removed, enable held low. DC/common-mode startup/discharge diagnostic only, not RF acquisition or timing qualification.

attached_core_source_demand.scope: Finite RX bias output current; excludes passive bleed/displacement. Not a transistor implementation.

bandwidth_sweep.scope: Nominal small-signal sweep only; lumped package probes and behavioral core boundary, no process/package tolerance or extracted distributed resistance.

active.scope: Independent linearized operating point with actual pad and retained network topology. Unit differential core stimulus for TX, external stimulus for RX/reference; disabled TX command transfer is zero by construction; missing driver parasitic feedthrough is not isolation evidence. Core impedances remain declared assumptions.

limitations: Physical pad devices and extracted capacitance are connected; full distributed interconnect R is absent. Optional segmented metal estimate is identified separately.
Capacitance/DC probes leave the attached core absent; transfer/lifecycle probes include its declared load.
Core input capacitance, finite off impedance and bias behavior are declared fixtures, not extracted core circuitry.
Reference bias remains ideal; RX bias and TX output use finite supply-connected boundaries. TX command sources carry no load. None is implemented core circuitry.
Differential RF match does not establish common-mode or DC impedance. The split resistive RX fixture remains a conservative loading assumption, not the planned common-source LNA topology.
Passive pad has no digital reset; disabled/reset differ only through the attached core controls.
External network and capacitor/inductor state persist through all transitions.
An 80ns run does not establish slow bias/coupling settling: 10nF with the reference bias path has an approximately millisecond time constant.
Odd/common capacitance includes protection and physical wiring; do not add the assigned budget again.
VSS current includes displacement and declared core-load current, not only protection conduction.
Input protection has no demonstrated positive ESD trigger/survival; no ESD qualification.
Receiver sensitivity, additive jitter and RF output distortion require the actual attached core.
